beliefs.practice: Never hard-code the cluster connection string or keys in source; read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any keys) from environment variables or Azure Key Vault at runtime and keep only a .env.example placeholder in repo.

Create a single global MongoClient and reuse it for the lifetime of the process; do not instantiate a new client per request. Tune pool sizes (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) in the URI/options for expected concurrency.
Always connect with TLS/SSL enabled (e.g., include tls=true or ssl=true in the MongoDB URI) and validate server certificates unless explicitly using a trusted internal test endpoint.
Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors (HTTP 429, 503, network timeouts); respect Retry-After if returned by the server.

Store vector embeddings as a fixed-length float32 array with an explicit binary BSON subtype (use the provider-supported subtype, e.g., 0x09 if the server expects it), and record the embedding dimension in the document schema to validate clients (e.g., {embeddingDim:512}).

L2-normalize embeddings on the client (or store both normalized and raw) if you plan to use cosine similarity in the index, or ensure the index/index option explicitly selects the appropriate similarity (cosine vs. inner-product vs. L2).

When creating a vector index prefer an approximate index (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN) tuned for your workload: specify dimensions (512), index type (vector-ivf or hnsw), and index-specific parameters (e.g., nlist or ncentroids for IVF; M/efConstruction for HNSW) rather than using a default generic index.

Build vector indexes before bulk-loading production datasets and wait for the index build to complete (check listIndexes or server index status) — do not run heavy vector queries while index builds are in progress.
For bulk seeding use insert_many or bulk_write with ordered=False and reasonably sized batches (e.g., 500–5000 docs) to avoid memory/timeouts; avoid one-document inserts in loops.
Do not return the full embedding vector in API responses by default; project only required metadata and a score to minimize bandwidth and avoid leaking model outputs.

Put the $search (or provider vector-search) stage as the first stage in any aggregation pipeline if using a provider search aggregation API; many engines require the search stage to be first to produce relevance-ordered results.
When issuing a vector similarity query request, include a top-k limit (e.g., limit: 8) and use server-side scoring to return results in descending similarity order instead of sorting client-side.

If the provider supports it, prefer using a dedicated vector-search API/operator (e.g., a vendor-provided $search with vector clause) rather than brute-force client-side distance computation for performance and accuracy.

Tune collection/cluster throughput (RUs or instance tier) to account for the cost of vector queries and index build operations; use autoscale or provisioned capacity and monitor consumed throughput during indexing and queries.

For development and CI, keep credentials out of logs and sample data; provide a .env.example with placeholders and document how to set DOCUMENTDB_URI rather than providing real URIs in repository files.
Measure and compare approximate index recall by computing brute-force (CPU) top-K on a small validation set and compare to index results; adjust index params (nprobe, ef) if recall is too low.

When packing embeddings into BSON binary ensure byte order and type match server expectations (float32 little-endian); use a consistent serializer (e.g., numpy.astype('float32').tobytes()) and validate roundtrip reads in tests.
Avoid embedding large images/large blobs in the DB documents; store image URLs or use a dedicated blob store and index metadata/embeddings in DocumentDB only.

Log and capture server error payloads and query plans (explain) when a vector query fails; use the DB provider's explain or profile tools to diagnose requirements like whether $search must be the initial pipeline stage.

Protect the database at network level (IP firewall rules, private endpoints or VNet) and restrict the credentials to least privilege (database user scoped to sample_retail_11 rather than cluster admin).
